title: The Path Back Is Confession
summary: When our hearts grow cold, the way back is confession, to God and to one another, because our sins have not been brushed aside but paid for.
exhortation: Here we see the pathway back to restoration: confession. If you are struggling with a cold heart, if you feel distant from God, one of the main ways we end up in that place is unconfessed sin. And yet as Christians we have a grace so great that we can go to God at any time and confess our sins to him, because of what he has done for us on the cross by shedding his blood for our sin.

He is faithful and just. He's not just saying, "Okay, forget about it." He's saying, "I have paid for it." This is a just forgiveness he gives us, a just restoration. Our sins have not just been brushed aside. They have been paid for by the precious blood of Jesus.

There's another path here that I think is important. It says that when we walk in the light, we have fellowship with one another. I think this shows the importance of being in fellowship with each other. Maybe not for every single sin, but it can be important to confess to one another. You should have brothers and sisters in your life you can go to and confess your sin. That has a restoring effect that softens our hearts and warms them toward God.
So if you find yourself feeling distant and cold, consider this passage and remember that we have such a great grace. Our sins have been paid for, so we can confess.
prayer: Lord, thank you for the mercy of the cross. Thank you for your willingness to take the cross upon yourself. Every idol and false god of this world demands sacrifice, over and over and over again, more and more until it consumes us. But you, Jesus, are totally different. You gave yourself one time as the final, complete and totally sufficient sacrifice. So Jesus, we praise you and we thank you.

May we remember the grace of Jesus that is available to us. And if we are caught in any sin that is holding us and putting a barrier between us and you, may we run in repentance and find fresh mercy and grace at the foot of the cross. In Jesus' name, amen.
